summary: Turn localization commitments into partnership models, budgets, risk controls, and measures. Explore the practical five-day course.
lede: Humanitarian localization training helps partnership, programme, grants and donor teams translate locally led action commitments into practical operating decisions. It covers assessing partnership quality, mapping decision rights, analyzing partner budgets and indirect costs, managing shared risks, and selecting indicators to report progress and accountability.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for people responsible for humanitarian partnerships, locally led programme decisions, funding arrangements, accountability, and coordination across organizations.
modules: Capacity Strengthening and Locally Led Action
prerequisites: Recommended: practical exposure to humanitarian or social-protection programmes, NGO partnerships, grant management, donor reporting, or coordination. No coding or programming is required. Advanced measurement and reporting concepts are covered at an operational-application level; the course does not train you to build software or conduct an external organizational audit.
